newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 cashmere output seen at 10,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 cashmere output seen at 10,000 tonnes.

text.p: China's total cashmere output will reach 10,000 tonnes in 1996 while domestic demand for raw cashmere is estimated at 6,000-7,000 tonnes, the Economic Information Daily said on Thursday.
The newspaper gave no comparative figures for cashmere output and demand last year.
China is the world's largest producer of raw cashmere and cashmere products.
China currently has more than 2,000 small and medium-sized cashmere enterprises with a total annual output capacity of four million items using 6,000 tonnes of cashmere.

Output of sheep's wool in 1996 was forecast at more than 270,000 tonnes, of which 60,000 tonnes would come from Inner Mongolia, 1,000 tonnes more than in the same period last year, it said. China is a major wool importer.
